beats.text: In 1807, Napoleon Bonaparte went to battle against three thousand rabbits.
He had just defeated Russia and Prussia, so his generals threw a celebratory hunt.
His chief of staff, Berthier, packed three thousand cages onto a sunny French field.
When the cages opened, the rabbits didn't run away.
They formed a solid wall of fur and charged straight at Napoleon.
Luckily, the Emperor laughed and swatted them back with his riding crop.
Unluckily, there were three thousand of them, and they flanked his boots.
You see, Berthier hadn't caught wild hares, he bought tame farm rabbits.
To them, a man in a coat wasn't a hunter, he was the waiter bringing cabbage.
Soon they were climbing his jacket, chewing his buttons, and swarming his generals.
Napoleon sprinted backward to his royal carriage and slammed the door.
The rabbits chased the wheels down the road and leapt through the windows.
The French army retreated. The rabbits stayed.
And the man who conquered Europe was defeated by dinner time.
